stories.title: SBPL turns 230: open house at the Central Library
stories.dek: Cake, rare books and behind-the-scenes tours to celebrate the third-oldest library system in the country.
body: Silverbrooks Public Library opened its doors in 1796, when the city was still a harbor town of a few thousand people. Two hundred thirty years later it serves all of metro Thompson County from 14 locations.

The open house runs all day at the Central Library. Staff will lead tours of the Albanardia history room, where the library keeps letters and maps from the Swedish and French settlers. Kids can make their own library card holder, and there is birthday cake at 2 PM while it lasts.
Every visitor who signs up for a new card on Saturday gets a limited-edition 1796 card design.

stories.title: Story time en français
stories.dek: Songs, rhymes and picture books in French for kids 5 and under.
body: Saint-Bruno's French-speaking families have kept the language alive for more than 300 years, and this weekly story time is one of the ways they do it. You don't need to speak French to come. Every book is shown with pictures, and the songs are easy to follow.
Story time runs about 30 minutes and ends with free play. Caregivers stay with their kids.

stories.title: Sailing knots workshop
stories.dek: Learn the bowline, cleat hitch and clove hitch from local sailing instructors.
body: In a city where most people learn to sail before they learn to drive, knowing your knots is basic literacy. Instructors from community sailing programs will teach the six knots every sailor uses, with rope for everyone to practice on.
The Pearl's End Branch holds the library's maritime and sailing collection, so you can check out a seamanship book on your way out.

stories.title: Maker lab: 3D printing basics
stories.dek: Design something small and print it on the Central Library printers.
body: The Central Library maker lab has three 3D printers that anyone with an SBPL card can use. This intro class covers the basics of free design software and how to send a print.
Each teen leaves with a small print they designed. Space is limited to 12, so sign up at the front desk.

stories.title: Mill Night lantern-making
stories.dek: Make a paper lantern to carry along the Wellington River on Mill Night.
body: Every November, Old Mill lights up the river with handmade lanterns. The Old Mill Branch, in a converted 1840s mill office, hosts a lantern-making afternoon the weekend before.
All supplies are provided. Lanterns use battery tea lights, so they are safe for kids to carry.

stories.title: Free homework help for grades 6–12
stories.dek: Drop-in tutoring in math, science, writing and French, four days a week.
body: Volunteer tutors, many of them students from McKay University, help with homework at the Lindgren Heights Branch Monday through Thursday after school.
No appointment is needed. Bring your assignment and an SBPS student ID or library card.

stories.title: Tour the Albanardia history room
stories.dek: See 18th-century maps, settler letters and the first edition of The Silverbrooks Times.
body: The history room on the Central Library's top floor holds the largest collection of Albanardia history anywhere. On this guided tour, a librarian brings out pieces that are usually kept in the vault, including a 1787 map of the harbor and the city's earliest library ledger.
Tours are limited to 20 people. Photos are allowed without flash.

stories.title: More eBooks and films than ever on Libby and Kanopy
stories.dek: SBPL added 8,000 eBooks and audiobooks this fall, with shorter hold waits on popular titles.
body: Your SBPL card works with the Libby app for eBooks and audiobooks and with Kanopy for films. This fall the library bought more copies of its most-requested titles, cutting the average hold wait by about a third.
Sign in to either app with your library card number and PIN.

stories.title: The Pearl's End School leads the Metro League sailing standings
stories.dek: With one regatta left in the fall season, the K-12 school from the oldest waterfront in the city is 17 points clear.
body: The Pearl's End School sits in first place in the Silverbrooks Metro League fall sailing standings with 41 points, ahead of McKay High School at 58. Sailing is scored like real regattas, where the lowest score wins.
Pearl's End sails out of the inner harbor, a few blocks from school. Coach says the team practices in almost any weather, including 48-degree frostbite days.
The final fall regatta is Saturday, Nov 14, on the harbor. Spectators can watch from the Pearl's End pier.

After-school programs and athletics practices are also canceled that day. Classes resume on Thursday, November 12.

body: Elementary and middle schools will have early dismissal on November 23, 24 and 25 for family conferences. Each family gets a 20-minute meeting with their child's teacher.
Your school will send a sign-up link. Interpreters are available in French, Swedish and other languages if you ask when you sign up.

stories.title: French immersion grows to three more elementary schools
stories.dek: Starting next fall, Saint-Paris, Ulvaeus and Old Mill families can choose French immersion for kindergarten.
body: French immersion has been offered in Saint-Bruno for generations, and every year the waitlist grows. The School Board voted 6-1 to add kindergarten immersion classes at one elementary school each in Saint-Paris, Ulvaeus and Old Mill.
Students in immersion learn most subjects in French through 5th grade, then continue at Saint-Bruno High School or any other SBPS high school.

body: Every SBPS student is assigned schools based on their neighborhood. Families can ask to transfer to a different school during the open window, January 5 to March 1.

stories.title: The D Line Now Ends Under the Terminal as SBX Rebuilds Its Front Door
stories.dek: A new transit center, a free shuttle to every concourse and a one-way Terminal Drive change how Silverbrooks gets to its airport.
body: A new transit center, a free shuttle to every concourse and a one-way Terminal Drive change how Silverbrooks gets to its airport.

For years, riders bound for Silverbrooks Thompson International stepped off the SBTrain D Line short of the terminal and wondered where the rest of the airport had gone. Starting this week, the D Line runs its last stretch under the garages and ends at the new SBX Transit Center, one escalator ride from check-in.

The center is now the single ground stop for the airport. The D Line, the SBMetro R Line, ALBExpress X4 to New Brolin, the 81 to Rutherford and the 110 SBX Flyer from Elliot Square all meet there. So does the AirLink people mover.

The SBX Airport Authority, which runs the airport separately from SBTransit, has launched the free SBX Terminal Shuttle. Buses leave the Transit Center every five minutes and circle to Concourse X (International), then A, B, C and D. “Nobody should walk a mile with a suitcase to find their gate,” an authority spokesperson said.

stories.dek: The SBX Transit Center sits inside Terminal Drive, between the short-term garages, and every train and bus that serves the airport now stops at its doors. Riders coming off the D Line climb one escalator to a single hall with ticket machines, an SBTransit service desk and the boarding area for the SBX Terminal Shuttle.
body: The SBX Transit Center sits inside Terminal Drive, between the short-term garages, and every train and bus that serves the airport now stops at its doors. Riders coming off the D Line climb one escalator to a single hall with ticket machines, an SBTransit service desk and the boarding area for the SBX Terminal Shuttle.

The shuttle is free and run by the SBX Airport Authority, not SBMetro, so it does not need a fare card. It circles the terminal counterclockwise with Terminal Drive traffic and stops at every concourse.

Airport officials said the loop takes about 13 minutes end to end at midday. Travelers headed to Concourse X for international flights reach it first, about five minutes after leaving the Transit Center.
Taxis and ride-hail pickups have moved to the outer curb on the east side of Terminal Drive, just past Concourse B. Drop-offs stay at the curb in front of each concourse.

stories.title: State finishes counting ballots from the November 3 election
stories.dek: County election offices have sent their final counts to the State Board of Elections, which will certify the results on November 24.
body: All counties in Albanardia have finished counting mail and provisional ballots from the November 3 general election. The State Board of Elections will meet on November 24 to certify the results.
Voters can check whether their ballot was counted with the ballot tracker on the elections page. Turnout statewide was the highest for a midterm election in more than a decade.

stories.title: ALBExpress winter schedule starts December 6
stories.dek: More X8 trips between Albanardia City and New Brolin, and later last trains on Fridays and Saturdays.
body: NETA will move ALBExpress to its winter schedule on Sunday, December 6. The X8, which opened this fall between Albanardia City, Ashton and New Brolin, gets four more round trips a day.
Last trains out of Silverbrooks on Friday and Saturday nights will leave at 12:40 a.m., an hour later than now, through the holidays. Printed timetables are at every staffed station.

stories.title: State parks switch to winter hours
stories.dek: Most Albanardia state parks now close at 5 p.m. through March. Day-use passes stay free on the first Sunday of each month.
body: Albanardia State Parks moved to winter hours on November 1. Gates now close at 5 p.m., and campgrounds at Cape Sturgeon and Hamilton Island are open on weekends only until April.
First Sunday free days continue all winter. Rangers lead a free winter bird walk along the Cape Sturgeon shore every Saturday at 9 a.m.

stories.title: Veterans Day: what's open and closed
stories.dek: City offices, libraries and schools close on Wednesday, November 11. SBTransit runs a Saturday schedule.
body: City Hall, all Silverbrooks Public Library branches and Silverbrooks Public Schools are closed on Wednesday, November 11, for Veterans Day. Garbage and recycling pickup is not affected.
SBMetro buses and SBTrain run a Saturday schedule. The Veterans Day ceremony starts at 11 a.m. at the memorial in Elliot Square.

stories.title: Leaf pickup starts in every neighborhood
stories.dek: Rake leaves to the curb on your normal garbage day. Crews will come through each neighborhood twice before December 18.
body: Silverbrooks Streets crews started fall leaf pickup this week. Rake leaves into a pile at the curb, not in the bike lane or over storm drains, on your normal garbage day.
Each neighborhood gets two passes before December 18. The schedule by neighborhood is on the Streets page, and you can report a missed pile through 311.

stories.title: Lantern Night tickets go on sale
stories.dek: Timed entry tickets for the December lantern walk through the Lantern Garden are on sale now. Residents get in free on opening night.
body: Tickets for Lantern Night are on sale for every night from December 4 to 20. Entry is timed every 15 minutes to keep the paths through the Lantern Garden from getting crowded.
Silverbrooks residents get in free on opening night with a library card. SBMetro will run extra buses to the garden on weekend evenings.

stories.title: D Line ridership jumps after the SBX terminal station opens
stories.dek: SBTransit counted 21 percent more weekday riders on the D Line in the first week after trains started ending under the airport terminal.
body: The D Line carried 21 percent more weekday riders last week than the same week a year ago, SBTransit said Monday, the first full week since trains began ending at the new station under the SBX terminal.
Most of the new riders got on or off at the airport. The free terminal shuttle carried about 4,000 people a day between the station and the concourses.
SBTransit says it will add two more trains during the morning rush in January if the numbers hold.

stories.title: Port of Silverbrooks breaks ground on a cold-storage terminal at Samolette
stories.dek: The new terminal will let fishing boats and refrigerated container ships unload at the same pier.
body: The Port of Silverbrooks started construction Friday on a cold-storage terminal at Samolette, its busiest container pier. The building will hold frozen seafood and produce before it moves inland by truck and rail.
Port officials said the terminal should open in late 2028 and bring about 150 permanent jobs. It follows a record October, when the port moved more containers than in any month in its history.

stories.title: Voyageurs stretch their win streak to four
stories.dek: Another win at AmEx Garden on Sunday keeps the Voyageurs on top of their division going into a road trip.
body: The Silverbrooks Voyageurs beat their division rival 3-1 at AmEx Garden on Sunday night for their fourth straight win. The Voyageurs scored twice in the second period and held on with a late penalty kill.
The team leaves Tuesday for a four-game road trip. The next home game is November 20.

stories.title: Mets hold off Aldense in front of a sellout crowd
stories.dek: UA Silverbrooks beat the Bruins 27-24 at Lindgren Stadium. Brady the Bruin made the trip, and so did about 3,000 Aldense fans.
body: UA Silverbrooks beat Aldense 27-24 on Saturday at Lindgren Stadium, stopping a last drive by the Bruins at the Mets' 20-yard line with under a minute left.
Aldense fans filled ALBExpress trains from New Brolin all morning, and Brady the Bruin greeted travelers at the SBX Airport station. The two schools meet again next fall in New Brolin.

stories.title: AlbTech demo night crowns a sailing startup
stories.dek: A team building low-cost race committee timing gear won the state student startup finals.
body: Ten AlbTech teams pitched at Wednesday's demo night, and the winner was a three-person team building low-cost timing and finish-line gear for youth sailing regattas.
The team gets $25,000 and a spot in the AlbTech incubator for spring. Second place went to a team making tools for nurses to track patient handoffs.

stories.title: Spring 2027 registration opens on every UA campus
stories.dek: Students can sign up for spring classes starting November 16. Seniors register first.
body: Spring 2027 registration opens November 16 on all five University of Albanardia campuses. Seniors register first, followed by juniors, sophomores and first-year students over the next two weeks.
Classes start January 19. Students can take classes at any UA campus and ride SBTransit and ALBExpress for free with a student ID.

stories.title: Lantern Night returns December 4
stories.dek: Thousands of lanterns light the Lantern Garden for two and a half weeks. Book a timed entry ticket before you go.
body: Lantern Night, Silverbrooks' winter festival of light, runs every evening from December 4 to 20 in the Lantern Garden. Paths wind past lanterns made by local schools, artists and the library's lantern-making nights.
Entry is timed, so book ahead. Dress warm, bring cash for cocoa and dock rolls from the food stands, and take SBMetro, which adds buses on weekend evenings.

stories.title: Oyster season is on at Pearl's End
stories.dek: The oyster boats are back on the water and the raw bars along the Pearl's End waterfront are shucking every day.
body: Fall is oyster season in Silverbrooks. After the Oyster Opening festival, the raw bars along the Pearl's End waterfront serve local oysters every day until spring.
Most places have a happy hour on weekdays. Walk the waterfront at sunset and watch the oyster boats come in.

stories.title: Holiday market opens in Elliot Square
stories.dek: Local makers, food stands and a skating rink fill Elliot Square on weekends from Thanksgiving to New Year.
body: The Elliot Square holiday market opens the Friday after Thanksgiving with more than 80 stands from local makers, bakers and farms, plus a small outdoor skating rink.
The market is open Friday to Sunday until December 31. The Capitol tree lighting is on opening night at 6 p.m.

stories.title: SBYC juniors close the fall season
stories.dek: The Silverbrooks Yacht Club junior team finished its fall racing season this weekend and moves to winter training on the water and in the clubhouse.
body: The SBYC junior racing team sailed its last fall regatta on Saturday in ILCAs, C420s and Optis. Coaches thanked the parents who ran the chase boats and the volunteers who kept the season going.

Winter training starts in December with weekend practices on the water when it's warm enough and rules and video sessions in the clubhouse when it isn't. New junior sailors are welcome; email the junior program through the club office.

stories.title: Haul-out weekend at SBYC
stories.dek: Members pulled boats, flushed engines and wrapped the fleet for winter in Silverbrooks.
body: More than half the members' boats at Silverbrooks Yacht Club came out of the water over haul-out weekend. Volunteers ran the crane, power-washed bottoms and helped wrap boats for the winter.
Boats staying in the water should have their winter lines and heaters checked by December 1. The yard stays open on weekends for winter projects.

stories.title: New Larssen boats join the SBCS fleet

body: Silverbrooks Community Sailing Center has ordered new Larssen Club Radials and Fyras from the Foxford boat works. They will join the fleet in the spring for classes, youth teams and member rentals.
The older boats will stay in service for beginner classes, and two will be donated to a school sailing program.

The center thanks its instructors, volunteers and donors, and will post the 2027 class schedule in January.

body: The first Larssen Optimists came off the line in Foxford this week. Larssen builds the Opti under license as an approved class builder, in club, race and pro versions.
The first boats are going to community sailing centers and junior programs that ordered over the summer. Every boat is measured and sealed at the factory, so it is class legal the day it ships.
See the Larssen Optimist for versions and pricing, and the Optimist parts page for sails, foils and spares.

stories.title: Hobie Wave, Hobie 16 and SailQube now at Larssen
stories.dek: Larssen now sells and services three boats from outside its own range, plus Hobie class parts.
body: Larssen now sells and services the Hobie Wave and Hobie 16 beach catamarans and the SailQube training pram.

The Hobie Wave is the easy, boomless family cat. The Hobie 16 is the classic trapeze racer with one of the biggest one-design fleets in the world. The SailQube is a tough, self-bailing pram for sailing schools.
Hobie Wave and Hobie 16 sails, spars, rudders, trampolines and covers are in the shop, on the new Hobie brand page.

stories.title: The Club 410 is here
stories.dek: Larssen's new collegiate doublehander takes the Club Radial idea and adds a bigger rig. Orders are open now.
body: The Club 410 is here. It is Larssen's new boat for college sailing: the same simple, tough team-boat idea as the Club Radial, with bigger sails and its own design.

The bigger rig gives college-weight crews more power and more to trim, while the boat stays quick to switch over between races and easy to keep running through a full season of team racing and fleet racing.
Teams can order the Club 410 with Fleet Sails: custom team sails with your school design, sail numbers and logo.
See the Club 410 page for specs and pricing, or request a fleet quote from the boat works at (302) 555-0144.

stories.title: The ILCA 4 MK2 sail is in stock
stories.dek: North, Hyde and Neil Pryde ILCA 4 MK2 sails are on the shelf in Foxford, with free sail numbers on every order.
body: The new ILCA 4 MK2 sail is here. Larssen now stocks it from all three approved sailmakers, North, Hyde and Neil Pryde, so youth sailors and their coaches can pick the loft they trust.
The MK2 is the class's updated radial-cut ILCA 4 sail, built to hold its shape longer than the original cross-cut sail. It fits the standard ILCA 4 rig with the same spars.
Every sail ships with free sail numbers. Add your country code for $10, and remember the ILCA format: any digits before the last four go in red, and the last four in black.
Order online, call the boat works at (302) 555-0144, or stop by 320 SE Marlin St in Foxford.

stories.title: The Harken MK2 vang for the ILCA is here
stories.dek: Buy it as a complete kit, piece by piece, or as a spliced TecPRO system from the Larssen Rig Shop.
body: Harken's MK2 vang for the ILCA is in stock in Foxford, and there are three ways to get one.
The complete kit has everything to swap your old vang for the MK2 in one box.
Separate parts let you upgrade one piece at a time or carry spares: the MK2 lower unit, the vang upgrade base, the upper block with key, the vang key and the quick pin for the MK2 tang.
The spliced system comes from the Larssen Rig Shop: a complete TecPRO vang built around the MK2 block, spliced, whipped and tested before it ships. There is also a Zircon edition.
Not sure which one you need? Send us your sail number and current setup through the custom rigging form in the Rig Shop.

stories.title: What's open and closed in Silverbrooks on Veterans Day
stories.dek: Schools, library branches and city offices are closed Wednesday. SBTransit is running its regular weekday schedule.
body: Silverbrooks Public Schools and every Silverbrooks Public Library branch are closed Wednesday for Veterans Day. City offices and state offices are closed too. Classes and normal hours resume Thursday.
SBMetro buses and SBTrain are running a regular weekday schedule. Parking meters on city streets are free for the day, and garbage and recycling pickup will run one day late through Saturday.
Federal offices, banks and post offices are closed. Most grocery stores, pharmacies and shops in Elliot Square are open normal hours.
A wreath ceremony starts at 11 a.m. in front of City Hall. The city asks people coming downtown to take SBTrain to Elliot Square, since street parking near the ceremony will be limited.

stories.title: Bauers fill the line as frostbite season opens on Silverbrooks Harbor
stories.dek: Forty-one boats raced Sunday in the first frostbite day of the winter, and the Larssen Bauer fleet was the biggest on the water.
body: Forty-one boats started the opening day of the winter frostbite series on Sunday off the harbor breakwater. The race committee ran five races in a southwest breeze that held between 12 and 16 knots.

The Larssen Bauer fleet had 17 boats, its largest turnout since the class started frostbiting here. ILCAs had 14 boats and Club 420s had 10. No boats capsized and no sailors needed help from the safety boats.
Starts were held twice for SBFerry crossings, as planned. Race officials said the delays added about 15 minutes to the day.
Racing continues every Sunday through March, with the first warning signal at 11 a.m. Drysuits or wetsuits are still required for every sailor.

stories.title: Winter heating help applications open
stories.dek: Households that need help paying heating bills this winter can apply now. Most payments go straight to the utility or fuel company.
body: The Albanardia Department of Social Services is taking applications for winter heating assistance through March 31. Help is based on household size and income, and it covers gas, electric, oil and propane heat.
Most approved households get one payment, sent directly to their utility or fuel company. Households with a shutoff notice can ask for an emergency review, which takes about two business days.
Apply online, by phone, or in person at any county social services office. Bring a recent heating bill and proof of income for everyone in the home.

stories.title: How to speak at Monday's rent hearing
stories.dek: The City Council takes public comment on rent rules Monday, November 16, at 6 p.m. Sign up at the door or send comments in writing.
body: The City Council will hold its public hearing on rent rules on Monday, November 16, at 6 p.m. in the Council Chamber at City Hall. Doors open at 5:15 p.m.
Speakers sign up at the door and get two minutes each. If more than 60 people sign up, the council will open an overflow room with a live video feed. Spanish and Mandarin interpreters will be there.
Written comments count the same as spoken ones. Send them to the City Clerk by noon on November 16. The hearing will stream live on the city's website.
SBMetro buses stop on both sides of City Hall. The council garage is free after 5 p.m.

stories.title: Voyageurs' win streak ends at four in road trip opener
stories.dek: The Voyageurs lost 4-2 on Wednesday night in the first of four road games. They still lead their division.
body: The Voyageurs' four-game winning streak ended Wednesday night with a 4-2 loss in the first game of a four-game road trip.
The Voyageurs trailed 3-0 after two periods. They scored twice in the third, but an empty-net goal with under a minute left closed it out.
The loss leaves the Voyageurs one point ahead in their division. They play again Friday, and return to AmEx Garden on November 21.

stories.title: Rent hearing Monday expected to fill City Hall
stories.dek: Tenant groups and landlords both plan to turn out for Monday's City Council hearing on rent rules. The city has set up an overflow room.
body: The City Council's public hearing on rent rules on Monday, November 16, is likely to be one of the biggest of the year. Tenant groups and a landlord association have both asked members to come and speak.
The council is weighing a cap on yearly rent increases and longer notice before big increases. No vote is planned Monday. Council members said they want to hear from residents first.
The hearing starts at 6 p.m. at City Hall. Each speaker gets two minutes. The city clerk will take written comments until noon that day, and the hearing will stream on the city's website.

stories.title: Saint-Marsé film week fills its screening hall every night
stories.dek: All six evenings of the European Film Week sold out their free tickets, and the university added a Saturday matinee.
body: Saint-Marsé's European Film Week drew full houses every night this week. Free tickets for each screening ran out within a day of being posted.

The university added a Saturday afternoon matinee to make room for more viewers. All films were shown in French with English subtitles, and faculty from the European Studies program led short talks after each one.
Organizers said they plan to make the film week a yearly event.

stories.title: UA campuses set Thanksgiving break hours
stories.dek: Classes break from November 25 to 29 on all five UA campuses. Libraries, dining halls and gyms run shorter hours.
body: There are no classes on any University of Albanardia campus from Wednesday, November 25, through Sunday, November 29. Classes start again Monday, November 30.

Residence halls stay open over the break. On each campus, one dining hall will stay open with shorter hours, and libraries and gyms close Thursday and Friday. The UA Medical Center clinic in Silverbrooks keeps its regular hours.
Students heading home can ride ALBExpress free with a student ID. NETA expects the Wednesday before Thanksgiving to be its busiest day of the year, so leave extra time.

stories.title: 2027 youth sailing grants open January 4
stories.dek: Clubs and community sailing centers can apply for up to $15,000 toward boats, coaches and scholarships.
body: The Northeastern Sailing Foundation will open its 2027 youth sailing grants on January 4. Applications close February 26, and decisions go out by April 1.

Grants can pay for new or used training boats, coach salaries, safety boats and scholarships. In 2026, NESF funded 19 programs, from new SailQube fleets at small sailing centers to a C420 team at a river club.
Programs that have never applied are encouraged to. NESF staff will review drafts through February.

stories.title: Club Race Officer seminar comes to Whilliker in January
stories.dek: Two days of US Sailing race management training at the Corinthian Yacht Club, January 23 and 24.
body: NESF will host a US Sailing Club Race Officer seminar at the Corinthian Yacht Club on January 23 and 24. The course covers setting courses, starting sequences, scoring and protest procedures, and ends with the certification test.
Every AYRC host club sends at least one volunteer, and NESF pays the course fee for anyone running a junior regatta in 2027. Lunch is provided both days.

stories.title: 2027 AYRC schedule: 11 regattas, opening May 22 in Foxford
stories.dek: The circuit runs from late spring to early fall, with a road trip to Barnegat Bay and the Championship back on Hanson Bay.
body: The 2027 Albanardia Youth Racing Circuit opens May 22 at the Foxford Yacht Club and closes September 25 with the AYRC Championship at the Silverbrooks Yacht Club.

Eleven venues host one regatta each. New this year are the Hamilton Island Ferry Regatta in July and the Pearl's End Harbor Regatta in September. The circuit also heads out of state for the first time, to Toms River Yacht Club on Barnegat Bay in New Jersey on August 14.
Sailors count their best seven regattas, and the Championship can't be dropped. Season registration opens March 1.

stories.title: Albanardia City wins the 2026 club team trophy
stories.dek: ACYC edged Silverbrooks by 24 points after a strong Championship weekend, with Corinthian third.
body: The Albanardia City Yacht Club won the 2026 AYRC club team trophy with 1,412 points, ahead of the Silverbrooks Yacht Club at 1,388 and the Corinthian Yacht Club at 1,240.
The race came down to the Championship, where ACYC put three C420 teams and two ILCA 6 sailors in the top ten. Foxford finished fourth, led by a deep Optimist team.
Trophies were presented at the NESF Awards Dinner. Thirteen clubs and sailing centers scored points this season, the most since the circuit began.
